subject: Acme integration: model routing & policy config — post-call next steps

Subject: Post-call recap: integration scope & next steps

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Goals we heard
- Deliver a latency-sensitive assistant for customer support (95th pct target: 300ms on text-only flows)
- Use embeddings + reranker for doc search, and structured tool-calls for order lookups

Integration & architecture items
- SDK setup: we recommend starting with the Redwood JS SDK (npm install @redwood/inference) for web backend usage; we can provide quickstart snippets.
- Auth: options are API keys for rapid POC or OIDC with your IdP for production (we can support per-route service accounts).
- Model routing: plan to use a tiered routing policy — low-latency path to smaller/faster model for interactive UI, cost-conscious path for bulk batch work; automatic fallback chain if primary runs out of capacity.
- Structured output & tool calling: use our function-calling layer (we map outputs to JSON schema and validate server-side).
- Embeddings/rerankers: embeddings for indexing, then a lightweight reranker model in the short list (we typically run rerankers on CPU for cost efficiency).

Attachments: attaching the Redwood integration guide and a starter mutual action plan.

Proposed next steps
1) Technical deep-dive with your engs (30–45m) — can we schedule for Thu 12/17 or Fri 12/18?
2) Decide priority: embeddings + reranker vs structured tool-calls for MVP.
3) Share a list of security/compliance contacts (we’ll surface SOC2 + network requirements).

Thanks — I’ll loop in Dev for the tech notes below.

—

Thanks — some quick technical notes for the 12/17 deep-dive: 

SDK & auth\- - Quickstart: server-side (node) example: require('@redwood/inference').client({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
- For production we prefer OIDC (you can map your IdP to per-route roles). We support KMS-wrapped keys for customer-managed encryption.

Model routing & fallback\- - Suggest a policy where UI requests go to model: "redwood-llama-lite-8k" with latency threshold 250–350ms; if latency SLO breached or capacity constrained, fallback to "redwood-llama-4k-fast".
- Cost policy: tag routes with cost tiers (high, medium, low) and allow programmatic overrides for batch jobs.
- Region routing: route EU traffic to eu-west nodes by default, with automatic failover to US nodes only if region is fully saturated (obey data residency flag).

Embeddings & rerank\- - Index: use 1536-d embeddings for doc store. We recommend a two-stage approach: dense retrieval (approx nearest-neighbor) + lightweight reranker.
- Reranker: can run as a small GPU instance colocated with the index or as CPU for lower cost; CPU rerankers increase latency (~50–120ms) but lower cost.

Structured output/tool calling\- - Provide JSON schema validators on the server side; function-calling returns structured payloads with a confidence score and a verification step before hitting your downstream systems.

Attachment: architecture-diagram.png (high-level suggestion for routing + fallback).

I’ll prepare a short runbook we can share during the deep-dive.
